lines: This is the map of Pocket Ledger, a tiny expense app: each sphere is one of its parts, each line what one part does for another.
Three scripted demo agents, with no AI and no network, are working tickets on it: they walk to their parts, say what they find, and one finds a bug.

mascot: Hello! I'm your mascot. This is Metaform's demo map of Pocket Ledger, a tiny expense app.
Each figure is an agent working a ticket. The one at the amount parser is hunting a bug.
Click any sphere to read what that part does, and for whom.
The dots on the lines are the agents' reads reaching the parts they work on.
To map your own project, run metaform start in its folder.

tickets.title: Monthly totals come out a cent short
tickets.task: A 19.99 grocery bill shows as 19.98 in the October total. Find where the cent goes and say what fixes it.

script.say: A 19.99 bill shows as 19.98. A cent goes missing somewhere between typing it and totalling it.
The command line hands the typed amount to parse_amount before anything is stored. Looking there.

script.step: Traced the amount from the command line into parse_amount in ledger/amounts.py.

script.say: Here: int(float(text) * 100). In floating point 19.99 * 100 is 1998.9999, and int() cuts it to 1998.

script.step: Confirmed: parse_amount truncates, so 19.99 is stored as 1998 cents.

script.say: The report only adds the cents it is given, so every total inherits the lost cent. The fix belongs in parse_amount.

script.step: The report is correct; the cent is lost where the typed amount becomes cents.

script.say: Found it. Parse with Decimal and round to the cent instead of truncating. Closing the ticket.

done.resolution: parse_amount in ledger/amounts.py truncates float(text) * 100, so 19.99 becomes 1998 cents. Parse the text with decimal.Decimal and round to the cent instead.
done.why: The cent is lost where the typed amount becomes cents, and every total inherits it.

tickets.title: Show each category's share of the month
tickets.task: Beside each category's total, show its share of the month as a percentage.

script.say: Each category's share of the month. First, what the report gives back.
month_totals returns whole cents per category, so the shares can be worked out from it without losing a cent.
The command line prints each total with format_cents. The share fits in the same line, after the amount.

script.step: The report already returns cents per category; the share is each total over the month's total.

script.say: Noting for the next agent here that the report works in cents and leaves the formatting to the command line.

remember.name: monthly report works in whole cents
observations: month_totals returns cents per category; ledger/cli.py formats them with format_cents and prints the lines.

script.say: Planned: the command line divides each total by the month's total and prints a whole percent beside it.

script.step: Planned the share column in ledger/cli.py; month_totals stays as it is.

done.resolution: Planned: ledger/cli.py prints each category's share, its total over the month's total as a whole percent; month_totals is unchanged.
done.why: The report already gives exact cents, so the share is a display change only.

tickets.title: A crash while saving can empty the ledger
tickets.task: Ledger.append rewrites ledger.json in place. Check what a crash halfway through the write leaves behind.

script.say: Checking what a crash in the middle of a save does to ledger.json.
append rewrites the whole file with write_text. A crash halfway leaves it cut short, and every entry is lost.

script.step: append writes ledger.json in place; an interrupted write truncates the only copy.

script.say: Safer: write the entries to ledger.json.tmp, then os.replace it over ledger.json in one step.

remember.name: ledger.json has one copy
observations: Ledger.append rewrites ledger.json in place with write_text; there is no backup or temporary file.

script.say: Recorded that here for whoever works on the store next. The command line needs no change.

script.step: The fix is in Ledger.append alone: write a temporary file and replace ledger.json with it.

done.resolution: Ledger.append should write ledger.json.tmp and os.replace it over ledger.json, so a crash leaves the old file whole.
done.why: Replacing a file is one step on every system; rewriting it in place is not.
